_what_this_is: Branch B task configuration: how one (basin, seed) quasi-harmonic trajectory is
placed on a machine. The SCIENCE settings are NOT here -- the timestep, the
friction, the temperature, the sampling interval and the three prohibitions live in
and the standard state lives in configs/openqha.yaml.
That split is the point of branch E: choosing a machine must never change a result.
If a value appears both here and in one of those files, that file wins and this one
_granularity_why: The protocol is 3 independent seeds per basin, because the seed-to-seed spread IS
acceptance criterion 5 -- the blank control that decides whether branch B can
measure an edge at all. So the independent work exists by construction and there is
never a reason to look for parallelism inside one trajectory.
A trajectory is also the smallest unit that can be resumed: the driver flushes
frames in chunks and rereads them on restart, so a task that is killed costs at most

_device_why: CPU, and this is a decision with a condition attached rather than a preference.
A GPU is worth it once structures are evaluated in
batches; a Langevin trajectory is a serial chain of single-structure force calls,
which is the case measured as not filling a card. On this repo's T400 the
same trajectory ran 3.5x SLOWER than on the CPU (394 s against 1393 s).
Revisit only when a batched interface exists -- not before.
_threads_why: 1, not 4. MACE thread scaling on a 10-atom molecule is 111/90/72/101 ms at
1/2/4/8 threads: four threads buy 1.54x while four separate
trajectories buy 4x, and eight threads are slower than four. Branch A uses 4
threads per task because CREST parallelises its own metadynamics runs; the two
branches divide the cores differently and the executors are not interchangeable.

_why: The driver takes --wall-budget-s and stops at a chunk boundary once it is past,
leaving a resumable state, rather than being killed with frames still in memory
(branch E acceptance criterion 2). Resource configs set the budget to 90
per cent of the job walltime; the remaining 10 per cent is the final flush.
per_task_timeout_s = 0 means no hard timeout: a trajectory that is going slowly is

A trajectory that fails the molecular-integrity check has fallen apart, and
rerunning it from the same basin with the same seed will do it again. Cluster
resource configs raise this to 1 for pre-emption, which is not reproducible.
There is no fallback of any kind. Branch B has three prohibitions and a driver
that writes them into every trajectory's metadata, where openqha/qha.py checks
them; a fallback that quietly changed one would produce a healthy-looking entropy

_note: Placement must not change a number, so branch E's criteria for this stage are about
the trajectories meaning the same thing wherever they ran. The scientific criteria
are branch B's, and scripts/production/s0_B_qha_analyse.py tests all of them.
Ask first whether the chain has a random step. It has two.
The seed fixes both, so the SAME machine reproduces a trajectory exactly. A
DIFFERENT machine does not, and demanding that it should would be a criterion that
cannot pass -- molecular dynamics is chaotic, and a last-bit difference in one MACE
force call (a different BLAS, a different core count, a different CPU) separates two
trajectories exponentially. Within a few picoseconds they are different samples of
the same distribution, which is exactly what three seeds already are.
acceptance.same_machine_same_seed: a (basin, seed) rerun on the same machine reproduces frames.npy byte for byte
acceptance.cross_machine: T*S_QH from the same (basin, seed) on another machine must agree within the seed-to-seed noise floor that acceptance criterion 5 measures -- the machine must not be distinguishable from a seed
acceptance.resume_is_seamless: a task killed mid-run and restarted must give the same frames as one that ran straight through on that machine: the restart reloads frames.npy and continues, so this tests the chunking rather than the physics
acceptance.identity_assertion: every trajectory's metadata passes qha.assert_trajectory_identity, or the analysis refuses it
